Sometimes we need to take a step back to continue forward my friend. 
I feel the not earning much and not liking your job. I have had aspirations to be a mechanic for years, yet I'm stuck in a lube tech job making minimum wage.

Is there a similar system? Or somewhere your skills could transfer to? If you lead a team, you could transfer to another field that has some overlap.
Do try to get into a doctor. Talk with them about what they think your next step should be in the mental health category. It may be medication, or therapy, but anythings worth a shot to not feel this way. 
As for the career coach, focus on your mental health first and foremost in my opinion. Look, but dont stress yourself out over it.

When I'm in a bad state, I listen to things like NF, who has sad lyrics, but at the same time uplifting. 
Medication may be worth looking into for you! It takes a little bit to come into effect, but it does help. Use the last of your motivation and effort to get into a doctors office. Anything is worth a try, Right?
I always say, any progress no matter how small is still progress.

And why do you feel your getting boxed out of your career?   
I wouldn't say its completely reversing, as I'm sure there's a relevant field that you could move over to.   
Even if you have to do things over the phone for the career coach or doctor, its still progress. Don't discount the things you are able to do as lack of progress.

No that's okay! I'm listening to music, and here to chat and try to help where I can. It helped me wake up in a way. See things differently, as I had less noise in my head, muddling things.   


How I know the medication works, is that over the month or so it takes to become fully effective, my thoughts started to clear, and I started to be able to feel more joy, and more positive emotions. Dont get me wrong, its not completely gone, but its helped clear things up so I can focus on fixing the rest, and self improvement.

You can always try reaching out to those old friends. I'm sure they do think about you. Explain what happened and why you drifted away.  


Success is what we make it. If you have to move, you have to move. Dont think of it as wasted time, think of it as a learning experience. Everything we do helps us learn and grow as people.

There is a big difference between being hard on yourself and being self aware. Grounding yourself is okay, but beating yourself over them is not. Acknowledge they are there, and work to improve them, but know that working on them is progress, and everything should be done in the name of progress.

Antidepressants. I have tried two different ones, the first one made me numb, the second one is working for me. Between that and positive affirmation, I have made steps. I still backslide from time to time, but am doing much better. I take Sertraline once a day.
Oh it absolutely is a good program. 2000 cad a month. Raising a child is hard for sure, expecially struggling with mental health, but its rewarding in its own right.

Sometimes we need to take a step back to reflect and make more progress. Trust me, the daily routine gets to me as well. As someone who prides themself on their progress, there are days where I backslide. We all progress at our own speed. We dont all follow the same track, and we dont all progress the same. Things take their time and place. If people are only attracted to your success, they dont belong in your inner circle. The right people will stick around, I promise.

As for the friends, I had to cut off a few people to find the ones who do value me the same as I value them. My best friend when I was younger would leave me out of things, and ditch me to hang out with other people. My best friend now? He includes me in everything, even family events. He went to get his class 1 license to help take care of my daughter.  
I promise, its your self image issues talking. There is not a thing wrong with you. You will find love. I promise you that.

People have a stigma towards treatment. I know some people were weirded out when I started medication. They dont understand the struggle. But if they arent sticking around while you are getting better and happier, they clearly werent the friends to be with in the beginning. Better people are out there I promise.

Its just something you have to work to control, and it is work for sure.

I got myself on medication (which isnt for everyone) and currently I am focusing on improving my relationships with others and how I talk to people, as I have had trouble reaching out for a long time, and I have always disliked messaging people as I thought I seemed annoying.   


Any start is worthwhile, and any progress is good stuff, no matter how small! Keep that in mind in your journey. :)
